Voat might be the chance to once again be a small (but quality) community. If you are a newlycommer, here are the biggest differences between the early days of nofap and what it is now:

Early days: people using their newly-found confidence, energy and free time to start a business, go after a childhood dream, learning new languages, learning new skills (a lot of piano players on the good ol nofap :)).

Nowadays it seems like everyone does it to get female attention. I absolutely support that; girls > fapping, no-one is contesting that. But I feel like at the beginning we aimed higher.

When I first started nofap I was just moving out of my abusive parents' home. I overcame a near-suicidal depression, found a job as a software developer, built 20+lb of muscle, while losing body fat, started playing jazz piano (still a beginner ;() and I'm now creating a side-income that might become my own business in a few years. Funny thing is, there used to be some guys who had the exact same accomplishments - an actual 100% match. Many quit their jobs after being successful in what actually made them happy and I hope I'll follow them.

And these are not superpowers. This outcome is expected once you learn the self-discipline required to stick to nofap for 100+ days. Every small further success increases your motivation further, the gym keeps you more energetic and the creative hobbies help you rest better and appreciate little things more.

A creative hobby, a hobby that makes you money and a hobby that keeps you fit are the standard next steps.

But for me the snowball that turned into this avalanche was indeed NoFap.

Girls are just your next reward :)

5 reasons why Target sold pharmacy business to CVS for $1.9 billion

This is the biggest news and commerce story of the day. Target is having competitive pressure from Best Buy and Walmart. The Pharmacy business at Target is likely a marginal business.

Conversely, in our area, the CVS is heavily focused on the medical space and is not very "retail" driven. I have seen other states where Longs Drugs name was retained and the retail space was stronger (Hawaii).

It feels like this is a step towards a merger of CVS and Target.

Certainly, in the context of pharmacy and prescription drug distribution, CVS Caremark is now the biggest player in the space. It virtually dominates the prescription pharmacy space.

I would go so far as to state that in some areas, the CVS momentum is so strong that deals like this should face increased scrutiny from DOJ on anti-trust review.

Since CVS is acquiring the Target pharmacy database, CVS is basically in a position to dictate the contract terms to Target Pharmacy. Therefore, there is no choice of Target. They must sell to CVS or their whole pharmacy operation becomes a cash loser, as the story states.

CVS has the ability to see every prescription filled at every CVS pharmacy, every Longs Drugs, every Target Pharmacy, and due to Caremark, nearly every prescription filled under a Caremark contract at any independent pharmacy.

CVS Caremark is too large!
